learning_objective: 🎯 Master the logic of English Syntax (Sentence Structure) to unjumble words flawlessly, and learn to transform sentences (change their form) without changing their original meaning!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: English strictly follows the S-V-O pattern: Subject (Who/What does the action) + Verb (The action) + Object (Who/What receives the action) + Place + Time. Example Jumbled: 'in the park / played / boys / cricket / yesterday'. Ordered: 'Boys (S) played (V) cricket (O) in the park (Place) yesterday (Time).'
Removing 'too'. Example: 'He is too weak to walk.' Transformation: 'He is SO weak THAT he CANNOT walk.' (Use 'cannot' for Present tense, 'could not' for Past tense).

Changing the adjective degree without changing the meaning. 
Superlative: 'Iron is the most useful metal.' 
Comparative: 'Iron is more useful than any other metal.' 
Positive: 'No other metal is as useful as iron.'

Use 'Not' + Opposite word. Example: 'He is honest' ➔ 'He is not dishonest.' 
Use 'As soon as' ➔ 'No sooner...than'. Example: 'As soon as he saw the tiger, he ran.' ➔ 'No sooner did he see the tiger than he ran.'

fun_activity.title: 🧩 Sentence Jigsaw Puzzle
fun_activity.instructions: Reordering is just a jigsaw puzzle! Always find the VERB (action) first. Ask 'Who did it?' -> That's your Subject. Ask 'Did what?' -> That's your Object. Example: 'apple / ate / the / boy / an'. Verb = ate. Who ate? The boy. Ate what? An apple. Result: 'The boy ate an apple.' Easy!

exam_tips: 📌 In reordering, if it's an Interrogative (Question) sentence, start with the 'Wh-word' or 'Helping Verb' (Is, Am, Are, Do, Does) + Subject + Main Verb.
📌 Rule for 'No sooner...than': Inversion occurs! It is followed by 'did + Subject + V1' or 'had + Subject + V3'. (e.g., 'No sooner DID the bell RING THAN the students rushed out.').
📌 When changing Exclamatory to Assertive: 'What a beautiful flower it is!' becomes 'It is a very beautiful flower.'
quick_recap: ⭐ Sentence structure logic: Subject + Verb + Object + How (Manner) + Where (Place) + When (Time).
⭐ Removing 'too' changes a simple sentence into a complex sentence with 'so...that'.
⭐ 'As...as' is used in Positive degree (As tall as), while 'than' is used in Comparative degree (Taller than).
